full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 266

Huang v. Mou Credit Management Co., Ltd. — dispute over personal information protection

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on August 28, 2025)

Keywords: civil; personal information protection; Use Now, Pay Later; credit service; necessity principle; least impact

Ruling Gist

The "Use Now, Pay Later" function requires the activation of a credit service as a necessary condition. Collecting personal information that reflects the user's personal credit or risk status by the relevant credit service provider falls within the scope of "necessary for the conclusion or performance of a contract to which the individual is a party." To provide the "Use Now, Pay Later" service, the credit service provider collects the user's relevant credit information in a manner that has the least impact on the individual's rights and interests, and has fulfilled its obligation to inform the user regarding the collection of personal information. If the user claims that such collection infringes upon their personal information rights and interests, the People's Court shall not support such claim in accordance with the law.

Basic Facts

On March 15, 2021, Huang discovered that a credit account had been activated without his permission. Upon inquiry with the customer service of the credit account operator, Mou Credit Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Mou Credit"), Huang was informed that this was due to his use of the "Use Now, Pay Later" function when activating the Chongqing public transportation ride code on March 7, 2021 via a certain application. Specifically, when activating the Chongqing public transportation ride code through a certain application, it was necessary to click "Agree to the Agreement and Activate," below which there was text in blue font stating: "View 'the Certain Application Chongqing Public Transportation Payment Service Agreement,' 'the Certain Service Agreement,' and 'the User Authorization Agreement'; authorize the Chongqing public transportation ride code to obtain your name, phone number, and ID number for real-name card issuance." The Certain Application Chongqing Public Transportation Payment Service Agreement stated that the public transportation payment service is provided to users jointly by Mou (Hangzhou) Information Technology Co., Ltd. and Mou (China) Network Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter collectively referred to as "Mou Technology Company"). When certain conditions are met and the user is unable to pay the fare in a timely manner, Mou Technology Company will advance the fare on behalf of the user and acquire the creditor's right to claim and recover the fare from the user. The user must agree to authorize Mou Technology Company to query the user's credit score as a risk assessment reference for the activation and continued provision of the public transportation payment service. The Certain Service Agreement stipulated that the user authorizes Mou Credit to collect and process information from information providers who lawfully possess the user's personal information. The scope of collected information may include personal identity information, transaction information, performance information, device information, and other information that can evaluate and reflect the user's credit or risk status. Huang then requested customer service of Mou Credit to close his credit account and delete the relevant personal information. Subsequently, Huang's credit account was cancelled and the relevant personal information was deleted.

On March 25, 2021, Huang activated the electronic bus card for Qingyuan City, Guangdong Province through a certain application, and reviewed the relevant service agreements. Among them, the "Mou Bus Payment Service Agreement" and "Mou Service Agreement" were both marked in blue font and could be clicked to view. The content of these agreements was substantially the same as the agreements for activating the Chongqing public transportation ride code. On April 25, 2021, Huang voluntarily cancelled his credit account.

On October 13, 2021, Huang filed a lawsuit on the grounds of a dispute over personal information protection, alleging that Mou Credit had engaged in acts of misleading, coercing, and unnecessarily activating the credit service when he activated the ride code and the "Use Now, Pay Later" service. Huang requested the court to order Mou Credit to cease the infringing acts and to pay damages.

Judgment

The Hangzhou Internet Court rendered a civil judgment (〔2021〕Zhe 0192 Min Chu No. 8058) on April 6, 2022, dismissing all of Huang's claims. After the judgment was pronounced, neither party appealed, and the judgment became legally effective.

Reasoning

The focus of the dispute in this case is whether Mou Credit's collection of Huang's personal information when providing the "Use Now, Pay Later" function constituted an infringement.

First, the collection of the personal information involved in this case was necessary for the "Use Now, Pay Later" contract. In application scenarios such as the electronic bus ride code, "ride now, pay later" (i.e., "Use Now, Pay Later") is a service provided by business entities based on the user's choice. It constitutes a reasonable use of data carrying personal information and represents an innovative commercial application of the credit mechanism. In this case, the "Use Now, Pay Later" function provided by Mou Credit helps third parties reduce the risk of financial loss caused by users' failure to pay fares, meaning it prompts users who have not paid fares to repay. In this process, the Mou Credit service primarily performs three functions: (1) Mou Credit provides bus companies and Mou Technology Company with the user's credit and risk status based on its operated Mou Credit service evaluation system; (2) Mou Credit receives the user's ride order information and payment status pushed synchronously by the bus company and Mou Technology Company, further accumulates order information, and analyzes the user's performance ability; (3) the bus company and Mou Technology Company push repayment information to non-performing users through the Mou Credit service. Since the "Use Now, Pay Later" function involves the third-party platform advancing funds, the third-party platform obviously needs to assess the user's credit status before providing the service and make a decision on whether to provide the service accordingly, so as to ensure the realization of the creditor's right.

Given that the provisions of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China regarding the processing of personal information are relatively general, the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China had already been promulgated and implemented during the trial of this case. Therefore, the relevant spirit of the Personal Information Protection Law was referred to in the trial of this case. Article 13, paragraph 1 of the Personal Information Protection Law stipulates that "necessary for the conclusion or performance of a contract to which the individual is a party" is one of the circumstances under which personal information may be processed. As stated earlier, collecting the relevant information is clearly necessary for the conclusion and performance of the contract; in fact, it could have been done without the individual's consent. However, the bus company, Mou Technology Company, and Mou Credit adopted the method of obtaining the user's prior consent to collect the information, thereby protecting the user's rights and interests to the greatest extent.

Second, the collection of the personal information involved in this case fulfilled the statutory obligation to inform. According to the "inform-consent" rule under the Personal Information Protection Law, even if a personal information processor does not need to obtain the individual's consent to carry out personal information processing activities, it still needs to fulfill the obligation to inform. In this case, the electronic bus card involved was jointly launched by the bus company, Mou Technology Company, and Mou Credit. Huang needed to review the agreements before applying for the card. During this process, the relevant agreements were all prominently placed, using a font color different from the black text on the rest of the page, to remind the user to pay attention and review them. Moreover, in the contract text, the clauses on personal information processing were marked with obvious identifiers such as bold font, enlarged font size, and blue color that are sufficient to draw the user's attention. Therefore, Huang's claim that Mou Credit had misled him into activating the credit service cannot be sustained.

Third, there were no circumstances of misleading, coercion, or the like in the collection of the personal information involved. Huang claimed that the Mou Credit service was bundled with the electronic ride code, forcing him to activate it, which violated Article 9 of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests of the People's Republic of China concerning consumers' right to independently decide whether to purchase or not to purchase any service. As a consumer, Huang did indeed enjoy the right to choose independently. He could choose to pay the fare in cash, choose to use a physical bus card, or, of course, choose to use the electronic bus card involved. In this case, the bus company did not force him to choose the electronic bus card method. At the same time, the Electronic Bus Card Service Agreement clearly informed the user that if he did not wish to continue using the service, he could apply for card cancellation or stop using the service on the electronic bus card service page. The Certain Service Agreement also clearly informed the user that the user has the right to close the authorization through the path "My Account - My Credit - Credit Management - Authorization Management" under the certain application. It can be seen that both the bus company and Mou Credit granted the user the corresponding right to independently choose the service, and the user could also terminate the authorized use of his personal information in a relatively convenient manner.

Fourth, the collection of the personal information involved in this case complied with the principle of minimum necessity. Article 6 of the Personal Information Protection Law provides: "The processing of personal information shall have a clear and reasonable purpose and shall be directly related to the processing purpose, adopting methods that have the least impact on the rights and interests of the individual. The collection of personal information shall be limited to the minimum scope necessary to achieve the processing purpose, and excessive collection of personal information shall not be allowed." In this case, the Mou Credit service, by conducting a pre-service credit assessment of the user, provided the bus company only with the conclusive information of "whether to grant access," which was necessary to realize the "Use Now, Pay Later" function and complies with the principle of minimum necessity.

In summary, Mou Credit's processing of Huang's personal information did not violate legal provisions and did not constitute an infringement of Huang's personal information rights and interests.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 1035 of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China
Articles 6, 13, and 17 of the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China
